speakers.imageAlt: Leo standing as a creative storyteller
speakers.name: Leo

speakers.imageAlt: Mara standing as a warm Shepherd encourager
speakers.name: Mara

companionMoment.title: God Does Not Waste the Story

transcript.speaker: Leo
transcript.text: Your story is not just a timeline of events. It carries themes, wounds, provision, courage, and moments where God was writing more than you could see.

transcript.speaker: Mara
transcript.text: Hold it tenderly. Some memories need gratitude. Some need grief. Some need redemption language. Ask what God has been forming through the story, not only what happened in it.

teachingBlocks: This lesson introduces Why story matters as part of the Story movement of Discover Your Divine Design. It should give enough teaching to make the next reflection meaningful without overwhelming the learner.
The rhythm is steady: teach the idea, name what to notice, invite a small act of reflection, then attach the relevant workbook section at the bottom so progress is captured in one place.

care.connect: Name triumph, tragedy, joy, pain, and the moments that left a mark.
care.act: List major moments without forcing full meaning yet.
care.reflect: Notice which moments still carry emotion, gratitude, grief, courage, or questions.
care.explore: Ask where God may have been present even in places you could not see Him clearly then.

transcript.speaker: Elena
transcript.text: Desire can become noisy when it is ruled by fear, comparison, or ambition. But desire can also become a clue. companionMoment.title: Four Voices Before the Niche Declaration

transcript.speaker: Dydi
transcript.text: Before you draft the final declaration, gather the pieces slowly. Identity, story, expertise, desire, and gifts are not separate piles. They are becoming one faithful picture.

transcript.speaker: Daniel
transcript.text: And if the picture still feels incomplete, that is all right. Purpose often becomes clearer through obedience, not before it.

transcript.speaker: Naomi
transcript.text: Use plain words first. Do not try to make the sentence sound impressive. Make it honest, usable, and faithful to what you have actually discovered.

transcript.speaker: Marcus
transcript.text: Then give it structure. Who are you called to serve? What has God formed in you? What kind of good work is beginning to take shape?

transcript.speaker: Dydi
transcript.text: Let this be a working declaration, not a final prison. God can keep refining the language as you keep walking.

teachingBlocks: This Pathfinder moment turns the Niche chapter into language the learner can carry forward. The goal is not perfection; the goal is a faithful draft that captures what is becoming clear.
The mature version of this lesson should review saved reflections, surface repeated words, invite companion guidance, and preserve a draft line for the final niche declaration.

care.connect: Review what this chapter helped you notice before trying to make the line sound polished.
care.act: Draft the Pathfinder sentence in plain language you can carry forward.
care.reflect: Ask whether the draft feels honest, humble, and faithful to what God is showing you.
care.explore: Consider what this line may contribute to the final niche declaration.

prompts.label: I believe God created me…
prompts.helper: Use this space to write a sentence or paragraph that captures your true identity in Christ.

experience.purpose: Preserve this Pathfinder line so it can be pulled into the final niche builder.

unit.title: Congratulations
unit.lessonMainIdea: Close the Journey with prayer, celebration, and one concrete next step beyond the course.
teachingBlocks: The ending should feel like a commissioning, not a hard stop. The learner has gathered language, evidence, prayers, and next steps that now need to be lived.
This unit can point them toward their next faithful experiment, future coaching, a Camp Circle, or deeper work with the Field Guide.
